stem: During a school activity, Meena's teacher shows the class four places near their school in Jaipur and asks: which of these places can be called a habitat because an organism lives there and the place provides both living and non-living conditions needed for life? () A. An empty steel tiffin box kept in a cupboard, where no organism lives; B. The bark of a neem tree where ants and small insects live, and which gives them shelter, moisture and air; C. A clean glass bottle of drinking water sealed in the classroom, where nothing lives; D. A dry wall of the classroom with no plants or animals on it

options.text: An empty steel tiffin box kept in a cupboard, where no organism lives
The bark of a neem tree where ants and small insects live, and which gives them shelter, moisture and air
A clean sealed bottle of drinking water in the classroom, where nothing lives
A dry classroom wall with no plants or animals on it

teacher.key_rationale: A habitat is a place where an organism lives and which supplies living and non-living conditions (air, water, shelter, suitable temperature) for life. Only option B shows organisms actually living in the place (ants and insects on the neem bark) together with non-living support (shelter, moisture, air). Options A, C and D describe places with no organisms, so they fail the test. The small size of the tree bark does not disqualify it as a habitat.
